title: While You Sleep, It Grows
subtitle: The week ends where the farmer's work does — in rest
teaser: Jesus told a second seed parable: the farmer sleeps, and the earth produces all by itself. The seed you scattered this week grows the same way. Today, be the sleeping farmer.
theme: Sabbath — resting because the growth was never yours to force
framework: Mark 4:27 - the seed sprouts and grows, though he knows not how

modules.passage: Jesus also said, "The kingdom of God is like a man who scatters seed on the ground. Night and day he sleeps and wakes, and the seed sprouts and grows, though he knows not how. All by itself the earth produces a crop—first the stalk, then the head, then grain that ripens within. And as soon as the grain is ripe, he swings the sickle, because the harvest has come."
modules.transliteration: automatē hē gē karpophorei — "of itself, the earth brings forth fruit"
emphasis: Night and day he sleeps and wakes
All by itself the earth produces a crop
modules.scriptureContext: The companion parable to this week's — the same field, the same sickle, and a farmer whose main contribution, between sowing and harvest, is sleep.

modules.heading: The Farmer Who Slept
modules.content:
All week we have stood in the mixed field — the night enemy, the servants' itch, the withheld sickle, the promised shining. One question may still be working under your skin: if I am planted in this field to sow, how much of the harvest rides on me?

Jesus answered that in a second seed parable, and the answer is almost scandalous: the farmer scatters, and then he sleeps. Night and day, sleeping and waking, while the seed does something he cannot see, cannot rush, and — Mark says it plainly — cannot even explain. The Greek gives the earth a word we still use: automatē. Of itself. All by itself the ground produces — first the stalk, then the head, then the ripened grain — on a schedule no farmer set.

This is the seventh day of the week the way God built weeks: not a reward for finishing the work, but a confession about who was doing the deep work all along. You have spent six days learning to put the sickle down. Today, put down the hoe, the ledger, and the watch as well. Every seed you scattered this week — the word of witness, the prayer for the person you refused to write off — is in ground that keeps working while you sleep. The kingdom is growing in the field of the world right now, in lives you cannot see into, and it does not need you awake to do it. That is how grain works.

modules.inlineImageAlt: A farmer asleep under a tree at night while young shoots sprout from the dark rows on their own
modules.inlineImageCaption: The farmer sleeps, and the seed sprouts and grows — he himself does not know how.

modules.prompt: Where has growth clearly happened all by itself this season — automatē — in someone you had no power to change?

modules.heading: Sabbath

scripture_anchor.text: Night and day he sleeps and wakes, and the seed sprouts and grows, though he knows not how.

modules.invitation: Do one deliberately unproductive thing today — a walk without a phone, a nap without guilt, a meal that takes too long. While you do it, the field keeps growing. Let that be the point.
modules.prayerText: Lord of the harvest, the field is Yours, the timing is Yours, the sorting is Yours — and so is every seed I have scattered. Teach me the farmer's other skill: sleep. Amen.
